solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Declares about English people getting their own back?

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: to aver is to declare firmly

explanation.surface: Someone states things about English people taking revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declares' looks like the definition at the head of the clue, but it is wordplay; the definition is the question-marked description at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who take revenge are avengers; the question mark flags a definition by description.

clue.text: Celebrity royal: a snake!

parts.note: a celebrity is a VIP, a very important person
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so for a royal

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a famous royal is a treacherous person.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder of Britain belongs to this family of venomous serpents.

clue.text: Clear goal

definitions.meaning: clear as in profit left after deductions, take-home
in football the ball goes into the mesh of the goal

explanation.surface: A football commentator calls an obvious goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Net income is what is clear after tax; the mesh behind the posts stands for the goal itself.

clue.text: Medical procedure possibly reduced lameness on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run in the other direction
reduced means the word is cut down, losing letters from both ends

explanation.surface: A doctor muses whether some treatment would cut a patient's limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims lameness to AMENE; 'on reflection' turns AMENE round.
explanation.definitionFit: An injection of fluid into the bowel is one treatment a doctor may give, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: At heart, professional pride the making of these web designers

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged
the heart of a word is its central part, here its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A tribute saying professional pride is what makes good website designers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At heart' takes SS from the centre of professional; 'the making of' rearranges SS with PRIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: These creatures spin webs, so they are designers of webs in a literal sense.

clue.text: Loud expert features

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A noisy specialist is the main attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: One's features are eyes, nose and mouth, which together make up the visage.

clue.text: Dismiss kind, wildly passionate individual

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job
a brand is a kind or sort, as in a brand of humour

explanation.surface: Someone sacks a pleasant, hot-headed employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirring up trouble with fervour is called this, like a burning torch.

clue.text: Skipper can set about article after international award

indicators.note: after puts the second part behind the award in the answer

parts.note: a player chosen for a national team is awarded a cap

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a tin is a can
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A sports captain opens a tin after winning an international cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a noun, a tin, not a verb; a cap is awarded to a player picked for their national team.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper commands a ship or leads a team, the same role as its commander.

clue.text: See name for pet dog?

definitions.meaning: to see something is to notice or detect it
a classic name given to a spotted dog, as in children's picture books

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to look at what to call a family pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to see; a famous cartoon puppy bears this name.

clue.text: Happier somehow about start of Greek inscription

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the extra one
somehow suggests the letters arrive in some unspecified new order
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone feels more cheerful about the opening of a Greek text.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator rearranges HAPPIER to EPIRAPH, which 'about' puts round G.
explanation.definitionFit: A short quotation or carved line at the head of a book or building is this.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink put out near bowl

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pint of beer is placed beside a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark, sweetish beer, a classic of British pubs.

clue.text: Wine lover, extraordinary voracious creature

indicators.note: extraordinary, read as out of the ordinary, signals the letters are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: An exceptional wine enthusiast, described as a greedy beast.
explanation.definitionFit: This stocky carnivore of northern forests, also called the glutton, is famed for its appetite.

clue.text: Bill's the judge

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a magistrate

explanation.surface: A man named Bill is identified as the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's mouth is a bill; British slang calls a magistrate by the same word.

clue.text: Posh school transforming it's fourth famous actress

indicators.note: transforming its fourth letter means one letter in that position is changed for another

parts.note: Harrow is an expensive private school in north-west London

explanation.surface: A smart school changes something and produces a celebrated actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transforming it's fourth' swaps the fourth letter of HARROW, R, for L; the clue does not supply the L, which the definition must confirm. Harrow is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean, the platinum-blonde 1930s Hollywood star, bore this surname.

clue.text: States "I have a girl's name"?

parts.note: saying 'I have a name' is saying 'I am' that name
Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone declares that their name is a feminine one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have a girl's name' amounts to 'I am Erica', run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States are often called by the continent's name, so the States means the USA.

clue.text: Draw rib, shaped as old military plane

indicators.note: shaped as means the letters are formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a rib, forming the outline of a vintage aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A restored vintage combat aircraft, flown at air shows, is called this.

clue.text: Marks volunteers getting involved in crimes

indicators.note: getting involved in means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: sins are wrongdoings, crimes
TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers are implicated in criminal acts and get marked.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks such as blots or smudges are blemishes left on cloth or a surface.

clue.text: Celebrate increment, finally, in pay

indicators.note: in sets one piece inside the other

parts.note: a fee is a payment

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Workers celebrate a pay rise at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour or celebrate a person, laying on a festivity for them, is to make much of them in this way.

clue.text: Correctional centre in Hampshire media lambasts

indicators.note: the letters are found in the centre of the phrase, held within its words

explanation.surface: A news report that local press in Hampshire attack a correctional facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correctional centre' reads as a prison, but only 'Correctional' is the definition. Hampshire is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial work corrects faults, as in remedial teaching to put right shortfalls.

clue.text: Crazy bloke in charge

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A frantic man is running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied, wildly overexcited behaviour is described as crazy or frantic.

clue.text: Porter maybe astride queen and king's racehorse

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the beer spreads either side of the royals

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale
R, regina, stands for queen
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A porter carries a queen and king on his back towards a royal racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a carrier but is the beer. Arkle was a celebrated Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkle won three Cheltenham Gold Cups and is among the greatest jumps horses.

clue.text: One not serving polite Scotsman?

parts.note: civil means polite
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A courteous Scot who is not in the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not serving in the armed forces is a non-military member of the public.

clue.text: Saint from this country embraced by the French

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: le is French for the
for a British newspaper this country is the UK

explanation.surface: A British saint welcomed warmly by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: The gospel writer and physician is one of the evangelists, canonised as a saint.

clue.text: Boy's fast time — when failing to finish

indicators.note: failing to finish means the word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A boy's quick time when he fails to complete a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast time' looks like a quick result but is a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Len, short for Leonard, is a boy's name.

clue.text: Shut up? About time!

parts.note: C, circa, means about
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An impatient demand for silence: about time!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as an order to be quiet, but means to confine.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut up a bird or animal is to confine it behind bars in an enclosure.

clue.text: Need cart for transporting wine bottle?

indicators.note: transporting carries things to new places, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cart is needed to move a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass vessel into which wine is poured to separate it from sediment.
